title: Electrosteel Castings Ltd - 500128 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Ductile iron pipe demand has collapsed as JJM funds froze: Q4 volume down 21% YoY to 1.48 lakh t, FY26 down 25%, with management guiding FY27 dispatch to ~7.4 lakh t pipes and 13-14% EBITDA margin.

summary.headline: Electrosteel Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 6.5% and standalone Q4 PAT turned to a INR 10.7 crore loss on a 21% volume decline.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales volume of DI pipes, fittings and CI pipes fell 21% YoY to 1.48 lakh tons, and FY26 volume fell 25% to 5.84 lakh tons, driven by slower Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) spending. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA including other income was INR 99.3 crore (6.5% margin) with PAT of INR 15.9 crore; FY26 consolidated EBITDA was INR 573.6 crore (9.4%) and PAT INR 161.5 crore. Standalone Q4 EBITDA was INR 57 crore (4.7%) and PAT a loss of INR 10.7 crore, with an exceptional labour-code cost of about INR 38-40 crore. The Board cut the dividend payout from 140% to 90%, subject to shareholder approval. Management guided to about 7 lakh tons of pipe dispatches and 13-14% EBITDA margin in FY27, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,202 crore (LT INR 352 crore, ST INR 464 crore)

segments.name: Domestic DI pipes
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes fell sharply as JJM funds were blocked; management says JJM constituted 50-60% of industry demand and Electrosteel holds about 20-25% of domestic market share.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export pipe volumes rose 7% in FY26, with Middle East about 50% of exports; exports were about 23% of Q4 revenue and are guided to fall to 17-18%. Exports were 20-22% of sales per a later answer.

segments.name: Valves and T.I.S. Italy
segments.commentary: T.I.S. Italy acquired August 2025 posted CY25 revenue of about EUR 41 million (up 15%), with FY27 revenue guided to INR 440-450 crore and margin 14-15%; Indian valve manufacturing is in design/development stage.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pipe dispatch guided at about 7 lakh tons, including exports (about 7.4 lakh tons on a pipe-only basis, per a later answer).
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 13-14%, with slower Q1-Q2 and better Q3-Q4.
Management expects steady demand recovery from Q2 FY27 and a return to stronger performance in Q3-Q4 FY27; longer-term stable margin band cited as 14-16% (15-16% base case).
T.I.S. Italy revenue targeted to double in four years (about 20% CAGR), contributed by India, Middle East and Europe.
Paint business: five-year plan to reach about INR 600 crore revenue; INR 200 crore outlay over 1.5-2 years; bottom-line impact expected from FY29.
FY27 maintenance capex about INR 25-30 crore; paint and valve plants expected to need about INR 200-250 crore over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Installed DI pipe capacity cited at 8.5-9 lakh tons; FY27 manufacturing volume expected at about 7 lakh tons.
FY27 maintenance capex about INR 25-30 crore; new capex for paint plant and India valve plant still in design stage, with timing not finalised.
Planned paint plant and India valve plant combined capex estimated at INR 200-250 crore over about two years.

Coal block: hard costs announced and roughly in line with estimates; soft cost for shaft and inclines pending from the Ministry. Some JSW-related disbursement received for one asset, with more slowly expected.
demand_pricing: Order book is 4-5 months, similar to other manufacturers; management says about 3-3.5 million tons of JJM tenders are yet to be allocated or ordered.
JJM 2.0 approved with outlay of INR 8.69 lakh crore to December 2028; Centre share raised to INR 3.59 lakh crore from INR 2.08 lakh crore.
Management cites FY26 JJM disbursement of about INR 1,500 crore (corrected from INR 15,000 crore); West Bengal allocated about INR 2,700 crore; FY27 JJM budget INR 67,670 crore.

Cost pressures from war: freight, overseas coking coal, energy costs up about 70-80%, and diesel/petrol price hikes. Management says price pass-through takes about a quarter because of existing order book.
Management says JJM is 35-40% of Electrosteel's demand (versus 50-60% of industry demand).

qa_highlights.question: Is the demand fall a new normal, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to blocked central JJM funds after scrutiny over the past 1.5 years; it called current levels the 'rock bottom' and expects a return to a 15-16% EBITDA margin over time.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Middle East conflict on exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East was about 50% of exports and sales there are affected from March 2026; valve diversification is expected to cushion this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 7 lakh tons of pipe dispatch including exports, and consolidated EBITDA margin of 13-14%, with slower H1 and better H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the standalone Q4 loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss of tonnage, an exceptional cost of INR 38-40 crore from the new labour rules, and margin squeeze from weak demand, plus a narrower cost-to-realisation delta.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 trends continuing into Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing substantial has changed, about 45 days into the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the T.I.S. Italy and valves outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: T.I.S. Italy CY25 revenue of about EUR 41 million; FY27 guided to INR 440-450 crore at 14-15% margin; valves seen as the diversification lever.

risks_watch: Pace of JJM 2.0 fund release to states and whether tender allocation to EPC contractors converts to orders.
Middle East/US-Iran conflict affecting exports (about 50% of export base), freight, coking coal and energy costs, and ship movement delays.
Standalone finance costs and losses; standalone PBT loss of about INR 7 crore in Q4.
Pricing pass-through lag of about one quarter on cost increases.
Coal block soft-cost approval and JSW disbursement timing.
Dividend payout cut to 90% from 140%, pending shareholder approval.
Possible drought and energy security priorities diverting government spending, though management views this as a temporary delay of one or two quarters.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident on long-term JJM 2.0 demand and margin recovery but repeatedly stressed 'steady' rather than 'pedal to the metal' recovery and gave specific numbers only for FY27 guidance. Answers on the timing of the return to peak margins and on the coal block were more hedged.
key_quotes: In my opinion, most definitely this is not the new normal, this is the rock bottom.
So, I am fairly certain that we will go back to our older days of earning 15%-16% EBITDA level
Steady traction, sir, not pedal to the metal traction. We are considering, as we said, we are being cautiously optimistic, not overtly optimistic.
Our integrated manufacturing operations and strong distribution network continue to provide us with strategic advantages in serving both domestic and overseas markets.

adds.what: Paint plant and India valve plant (combined INR 200-250 crore capex, design stage, timing not finalised)

growth.why: FY27 pipe dispatch guided at about 7 lakh tons (versus FY26's 5.84 lakh tons, implying roughly 20% growth) with 13-14% consolidated EBITDA margin and recovery from Q3 FY27, backed by a 4-5 month order book and about 3-3.5 million tons of JJM tenders yet to be allocated, but no firm capacity additions; installed DI capacity is 8.5-9 lakh tons at only ~50% utilisation.
